PhysioConnect › Conditions we treat

Conditions our physiotherapists treat

PhysioConnect physiotherapists treat a wide range of orthopaedic, post-surgical, neurological and sports conditions, at home or over video.

Book on the website Get the Android app

Orthopaedic and spine care

Lower back pain, neck pain and cervical spondylosis, slip disc, sciatica, frozen shoulder and knee osteoarthritis. Treatment usually combines pain relief, manual therapy and a progressive exercise programme you continue between sessions.

Rehabilitation after surgery

Total knee replacement (TKR), total hip replacement (THR), ACL reconstruction and fractures. Home physiotherapy helps you regain movement and strength safely in the first weeks after surgery, when travelling to a clinic is hardest.

Neurological rehabilitation

Stroke and paralysis recovery, Parkinson's disease, Bell's palsy, neuropathy and balance problems. Regular sessions at home focus on movement, balance, walking and independence in daily activities.

Sports injuries

Ligament tears, muscle strains, tennis elbow and runner's knee, plus return-to-sport conditioning.

Elderly care and mobility

Fall prevention, joint stiffness, posture and strength to help older adults stay mobile and independent at home. Family members can book and track sessions for their parents from one account.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Your physiotherapist will assess you before recommending treatment.

How booking works

  1. Choose your care mode: a home visit at your doorstep or an online video session.
  2. Pick your city and area to see physiotherapists who serve your locality.
  3. Compare therapists: photo, qualifications, specialities, years of practice, patient reviews and the consultation fee, shown before you book.
  4. Choose a single session or a package of 5, 10 or 15 days, every day or on alternate days.
  5. Pay securely with UPI, card or net banking and get an instant confirmation.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a doctor's referral for physiotherapy?

You can book a physiotherapist directly for an assessment. If you have a referral, X-ray or MRI report from your orthopaedic doctor, share it with your physiotherapist at the first session.

How many physiotherapy sessions will I need?

It depends on your condition. Your physiotherapist assesses you in the first session and recommends a plan, which you can book as a 5, 10 or 15 day package.

Can physiotherapy be done at home after knee replacement surgery?

Yes. Home physiotherapy is common after knee and hip replacement because it avoids travel while walking is still difficult. Follow your surgeon's instructions on when to start.
